title: Writing the results note
objectives: Write a one-page results note, including what failed.
Run the engine end to end and generate the note from the run.

screens.title: Two notes, one study
screens.prose: Two researchers write up the same momentum study on `make_bars()`. A reviewer has five minutes and reads both.

hints.text: Which note lets the reviewer check its claims?
Note A's Sharpe: gross or net? Research or held out? Out of how many tries?
Note B states the method, both periods, the trial count and what failed.

screens.title: The template
screens.prose: The results note is one page with fixed headings, in an order a reviewer can rely on. Here are the seven headings, shuffled.
screens.question: Put the headings in order.

lines.text: Question: what was asked, and why it would pay
Data: source, seed or dates, research and held-out lengths
Method: rule, fills, costs, slippage, look-ahead check, held-out rule
Results: research against held out, against buy and hold
Trials: $N$, the best, the expected best under no edge
What failed: at least two concrete items
Next steps: what to test next, on new data

hints.text: A reader needs the question before the data.
Method comes before results; trials and failures qualify the results.
Question, Data, Method, Results, Trials, What failed, Next steps.

feedback.correct: The same seven headings, every study.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each section uses only what came before it.

explain.text: Each heading needs the ones above it: results mean nothing without the method, and trials and failures qualify the results. A fixed order lets a reviewer jump straight to Trials or What failed.

screens.title: Nothing failed
screens.prose:
A draft note for the same study ends like this:

```text
## Results
Research net Sharpe 0.55 (lookback 2).
## What failed
Nothing major.
```
screens.question: What is wrong with the draft?

options.text: Nothing: if the study worked, there is nothing to list
options.why: This study did not work held out. And every study tried things that were dropped: those go here.

options.text: It reports research only and hides the held-out loss under "nothing major"
It is too short: add the equity chart
options.why: A chart of research equity adds nothing honest. The missing held-out column does.

options.text: The Sharpe needs more decimal places
options.why: Precision is not the problem. The held-out result is missing.

hints.text: Which column of the results table is missing?
The held-out Sharpe was −0.45.
A note that shows research only and says nothing failed hides the one test that mattered.

feedback.correct: An empty What failed is a warning sign in itself.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the draft with what the run produced.

byKey.fine: You accepted an empty What failed. No honest study has one: something was tried and dropped, or something did not hold out.

explain.text: The draft reports only the research year and calls the held-out loss nothing. A reviewer reads an empty What failed as hiding something. The fix is the held-out column and the three failures from the last screen.

screens.title: A good held-out year
screens.prose: Edge case. Had research picked lookback 10, the held-out year would have shown a net Sharpe of 1.86. The note would then be tempted to claim a lot. From l9, one year's standard error is $\sqrt{(1 + SR^2/2)/T}$.
screens.question: What is the standard error of a one-year Sharpe of 1.86? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.correct: About 1.65: the 1.86 is barely one standard error from zero.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put $SR = 1.86$ and $T = 1$ into the formula.

byKey.one: That drops the $SR^2/2$ term, which matters at a Sharpe this high.

explain.text: A held-out 1.86 is only 1.1 standard errors above zero. So a good year earns the sentence "held out confirmed the sign", never "proved the edge". The note still states $N$ and the standard error.

screens.title: On real data
screens.prose: The same code runs on real prices with a few plain changes. Replace `make_bars` with `cached_fetch` (l2) around `yf.download(ticker, start=..., end=..., auto_adjust=False)`, cached to disk because yfinance breaks often. Or use Nasdaq Data Link (formerly Quandl), its key in an environment variable.

For more than one share, a point-in-time universe that includes delisted names

The API key written into the script so the study can be rerun

options.why: Real data peeks through your code exactly as seeded data does. Keep every test.

Splits and dividends, dead companies, and secrets.
Adjust for corporate actions, include delisted names, keep the held-out rule and keep keys out of the code.

widget.solution:
KEYS = ["ann_return", "ann_vol", "sharpe", "max_drawdown", "calmar", "turnover", "hit_rate", "beta"]

def results_note(m_in, m_out, n_trials, failures, expected_best=None):
    if not failures:
        raise ValueError("a results note must say what failed")
    lines = ["# Results note", "",
             "## Question", "Does a daily momentum rule on one share earn a net Sharpe worth trading?", "",
             "## Data", "Seeded make_bars, seed 2301, 1,260 days: research 1,008, held out 252.", "",
             "## Method", "Sign of the lookback return; next-open fills; costs in bp; look-ahead check; held-out year opened once.", "",
             "## Results", "| Metric | Research | Held out |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for k in KEYS:
        lines.append(f"| {k} | {m_in[k]:.2f} | {m_out[k]:.2f} |")
    trials = f"{n_trials} settings tried."
    if expected_best is not None:
        trials += f" Expected best under no edge: {expected_best:.2f}."
    lines += ["", "## Trials", trials, "", "## What failed"]
    lines += ["- " + f for f in failures]
    lines += ["", "## Next steps", "- Paper trade the frozen rule for a year before changing it."]
    return "\n".join(lines)

screens.question: Select all that apply: questions you should expect about it.

How do you know the engine never peeks at the future?

How many settings did you try?

options.why: Language choice rarely matters here. The panel probes whether the result is honest.

hints.text: Think back over the course's four levels.
Execution, bias, metrics and honest reporting each give one question.
Costs, look-ahead, the held-out year and $N$.

feedback.correct: Four questions, and the note answers each one.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Choose the questions about whether the result is honest.

explain.text: Each question maps to a section of the note and a test in the repository. Saying "held out it lost, and here is why" beats a Sharpe of 3.

quiz.prose: Edge case. A study's held-out year shows net Sharpe 1.5, after 20 settings tried. One year's standard error is about 1.35 at that Sharpe.
quiz.question: What may the note claim?

options.text: That the held-out year agreed in sign, with $N = 20$ and a standard error of 1.35 stated
That the edge is proved out of sample
options.why: 1.5 is about 1.1 standard errors from zero. One year cannot prove it.

options.text: That no failures need listing this time
options.why: Every study lists what was tried and dropped, good result or not.

feedback.correct: Claim no more than a year can show.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. How many standard errors from zero is 1.5?

explain.text: $1.5/1.35 = 1.1$ standard errors: encouraging, not proof. The note states the result, $N$ and the standard error, and its next step is more data.

quiz.question: Which setting do you state explicitly in the call?

`threads=True`

feedback.correct: Say it explicitly, so the study reruns the same.
